shortDescription.text: Quantum-vulnerable ECDSA: transaction and message signing (1 file(s))

fullDescription.text: 6 reference(s) to ECDSA across 1 file(s), e.g. core/src/main/kotlin/net/corda/core/crypto/internal/Secp256k1SupportProvider.kt:32. A CRQC derives the private key from a public key that is already known (on chain after the first spend, in reused addresses): funds and approvals controlled by these keys need a migration path. shortDescription.text: Key material stored in the application's database with no KMS or HSM (2 file(s))

fullDescription.text: Columns that hold key material (key_material, private_key; first in node/src/main/kotlin/net/corda/node/services/keys/BasicHSMKeyManagementService.kt, line 62) are part of the service's own data model, the service reads them back to decrypt or sign with them (node/src/main/kotlin/net/corda/node/services/persistence/AesDbEncryptionService.kt:65), and no KMS, HSM, secrets-vault service or custody API appears anywhere in the audited tree. Encryption: application code encrypts it before storing (node-api/src/main/kotlin/net/corda/nodeapi/internal/crypto/AesEncryption.kt:45). Keep signing keys in an HSM or a KMS that signs (or in an MPC or custody service) so they never leave it; if keys must be stored, use envelope encryption — a data key per record, wrapped by a KMS key whose use is logged and rate-limited. shortDescription.text: Quantum-vulnerable ECDSA key in certificate (Corda Node Root CA)

fullDescription.text: The certificate Corda Node Root CA uses a ECDSA secp256k1 public key, valid until 2026-07-17. ECDSA is broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC. Track in the PQC inventory; prefer short certificate lifetimes; follow CA/Browser Forum and NIST PQC transition guidance for ML-DSA certificates. This is a forward-looking risk that depends on the arrival of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC). No such computer is publicly known to exist today; the timeline is uncertain. It is not a present-day exploitable vulnerability.
